name: Information theory
strandNote: Optional for every quant role. For machine learning research roles, and for using and building AI tools with judgement.
description: Measure surprise in bits, compress with codes, see why cross-entropy and KL divergence are the losses of machine learning, and measure dependence in bits.

requires.why: Entropy is an expected value: the probability-weighted average of surprise.
Surprise in bits is a base 2 logarithm, converted from other bases.
Code screens use list comprehensions and compare floats with a tolerance.
Proves the KL divergence is never negative with Jensen's inequality.
Shows that maximising the likelihood is minimising the cross-entropy to the data.
Reads joint and marginal tables and tests independence, which mutual information measures in bits.

lessonNames.l11-features-and-lost-information: A feature, a label and lost information
lessonNames.l12-a-signal-and-tomorrow: What a signal says about tomorrow

lessonObjectives.l1-surprise-in-bits: Compute the surprise of an outcome in bits as $-\log_2 p$.
lessonObjectives.l2-average-surprise: Compute the entropy of a distribution and find when it is largest.
lessonObjectives.l3-codes-that-save-space: Build a Huffman code and compare its average length with the entropy.
lessonObjectives.l4-how-far-text-compresses: Estimate the bits per letter of a text from its letter counts, and see why no code beats the entropy.
lessonObjectives.l5-paying-for-the-wrong-model: Compute the cross-entropy: the average code length when we code with the wrong distribution.
lessonObjectives.l6-the-extra-bits: Derive from Jensen's inequality that the KL divergence is never negative, and compute it in bits.
lessonObjectives.l7-perplexity: Turn an average loss into a perplexity and read it as an effective number of choices.
lessonObjectives.l8-likelihood-is-cross-entropy: Show that maximising the likelihood minimises the cross-entropy to the data, in nats or in bits.
lessonObjectives.l9-information-shared: Compute the mutual information of two variables from their joint table as $H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y)$.
lessonObjectives.l10-dependence-as-divergence: Show that mutual information is the KL divergence between the joint and the product of the marginals, so it is zero exactly when they are independent.
lessonObjectives.l11-features-and-lost-information: Measure what a feature tells us about a label, and see why processing a feature can never add information.
lessonObjectives.l12-a-signal-and-tomorrow: Write an estimator of the information a discrete signal carries about the next return's sign, and correct its bias on short samples.
